A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PNS-based CoT optimization work. All 22 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison; retained text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original CoT optimization, in-context learning, and fine-tuning experiments in Tables 1–3, with PNS analyses and a case study in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds expert evaluations, validator accuracy tests, and additional baseline results in Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the PNS estimator, intervention strategies, and ICL/SFT pipeline are retained. Section 4.1 adds an explanation of repeated CoT sampling to improve sufficiency, documenting the existing sufficiency-optimization stage without establishing a revised underlying method.

E1.justification: Training sources and mathematical/commonsense reasoning coverage are unchanged. The new human evaluation uses GSM-8k, CommonsenseQA, and MATH-500; additional comparisons use these retained benchmarks. No new domain or task scenario is established.

E2.justification: Appendix K/Table 7 adds evaluated SPIRIT, ReAct, and Tree-of-Thoughts comparators across four models and three benchmarks, substantially broadening the comparison methods. SPIRIT and ToT were previously discussed but not evaluated against Ours-ICL. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces two substantial evaluation protocols: five experts judging 50 generated CoTs across three quality categories, and validator MAE against expert labels for Qwen-72B, Qwen-7B, and GPT-4o at k=1,3,5,10. These extend evaluation design; the added standard accuracy formula merely clarifies an existing metric.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained PNS plots and ICL case study, Appendix I evaluates whether generated reasoning is sufficient, necessary, or redundant. Appendix J tests validator reliability and sensitivity to model choice and rollout count. These add direct examinations of reasoning quality and measurement reliability.

E5.justification: Monte Carlo PNS estimation remains unchanged, and neither version reports uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or repeated-experiment/seed statistics. The new rollout-count sweep and point MAEs assess estimator accuracy without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and existing PNS plots retain their results. New Tables 5–7 report 42/50 CoTs judged sufficient and necessary, 3/50 insufficient, validator errors such as GPT-4o MAE 0.050 at k=10, and SPIRIT/ReAct/ToT results across retained model–dataset settings. Table 7 repeats existing Ours-ICL scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix H derives rollout and validation costs and an overall O(k n²) complexity under constant step-length and token-time assumptions. The causal definitions, identifiability lemmas, Theorem 1, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: integrating PNS into CoT, optimizing reasoning traces, and improving efficiency while preserving or improving accuracy through ICL and SFT. Added supporting evaluations do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2.2 newly explains filtering as a one-time curation cost and SFT as reshaping the training distribution, avoiding test-time rollouts. New appendix discussions interpret harder-task failures and the dependence of validator reliability on model strength and rollout count. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository pointer, explains sufficiency resampling, and clarifies that manually checked training traces were not edited. However, it removes v2's Appendix H disclosures of inference hardware, software versions, temperature/top-p, and approximate evaluation runtime. SFT hyperparameters and prompts remain documented, but reproducibility information is materially revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through a new causal-XAI subsection and connections to invariant learning, causal representations, information-theoretic CoT assessment, and ChessGPT. Thirteen references are added, including LENS, LEWIS, and ReAct. The retained Appendix F discussion is substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify sufficiency estimation, accuracy, and SFT interpretation. v3 adds acknowledgments, author contributions, and appendix sections, and updates author-role and conference information. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 5–7 are added for human judgments, validator MAE, and expanded comparisons. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, with relocation, resizing, and page reflow, notably around Figures 2–3 and Tables 2–3. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Beyond v2's retained benchmark tables and PNS plots, v3 supplies expert quality judgments, validator sensitivity tests, broader baselines, and explicit computational scaling. These strengthen the evidence and explain costs. The gain is limited by an underspecified human-rating protocol and the loss of v2's decoding, runtime, and software-environment details.
